title: Keep every workspace current from one console
summary: Bare ia outside a workspace now opens an all-workspaces view over the tracked list, and tab switches to it from a workspace's own view. Each row is read through that workspace's own ia, at most four at once, and is classed by the statuses its checks report. Select workspaces and batch one offer across them: each repository gets a new git worktree on a chore/ branch with no upstream, its package manager's install first, then the offer's steps rebuilt for the worktree, every path argument checked to stay inside it before each step runs, while the user's own checkout is touched only by git metadata operations. Afterwards each next step is a separate choice: commit as chore: <offer title>, push and open pull requests through gh when it is signed in, open a failed repository, or remove the worktrees and keep the branches. Nothing is pushed unless chosen. f finds workspaces in a folder to track, and config.json's worktreeRoot moves where the worktrees go. A batch never waits on an answer: its children run with no terminal (outside Windows), so a hook or a passphrase-protected signing key that asks through /dev/tty fails for its repository instead of prompting; git gets no terminal prompt and no askpass program; and ssh runs in batch mode (BatchMode=yes) unless you name your own ssh through GIT_SSH_COMMAND, GIT_SSH or core.sshCommand, so a remote that needs a passphrase, a password or a new host key fails for its repository. A command still running after 10 minutes is stopped. The preview refuses a repository whose default worktree place lies inside another work tree (a nested repository or a submodule) or where git cannot say, with worktreeRoot as the way out, a second workspace of one repository in the same batch, and a worktree inside another repository of the batch.
